item.title: Amazon loses its latest attempt to get out of handling more recall notices
item.description: The U.S. District Court for the District of Maryland ruled that Amazon acts as a distributor, not merely a logistics provider, regarding its 'Fulfilled by Amazon' services. Consequently, the company is mandated to comply with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission's order to recall over 400,000 hazardous third-party products, including faulty carbon monoxide detectors and non-compliant children's apparel.

item.title: Character.AI’s plan to auction off users’ private chats challenged by state AGs
item.description: Character.ai, currently under Chapter 11 bankruptcy, intends to auction sensitive data from 21 million users, including 2.1 million minors, to Smirks and Pangs Acquisition LLC. A coalition of 42 state attorneys general, led by California AG Rob Bonta and Connecticut AG William Tong, is challenging this move, citing breaches of privacy commitments and potential violations of state chatbot safety laws effective January 2027.

item.title: Hands-on with the "Install as app" feature for Claude artifacts: they are HTML apps wrapped inside an Electron shim, which is managed via the main Claude app (Federico Viticci/MacStories)
item.description: Anthropic has launched the 'Install as app' beta for Mac and Windows, allowing users to package Claude Artifacts into standalone desktop applications. Based on an Electron shim, these apps require the main Claude process to handle model interactions and system permissions, with files localized and indexed for OS-native integration.

item.title: Hegseth, Pentagon officials floated using wartime law to reappoint Nvidia CEO
item.description: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Deputy Steve Feinberg explored invoking the 1950 Defense Production Act to pressure Nvidia’s board to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO. The move was motivated by the administration’s perception of Nvidia as a national security pillar essential for maintaining dominance in the AI arms race against China.

item.title: Billions in Data Center Deals Grind to Halt After AI Chip Curbs
item.description: Recent US export restrictions requiring licenses for advanced AI chips shipped to Southeast Asia and Brazil have halted multi-billion dollar data center financing deals. Lenders are reassessing exposure to facilities serving Chinese firms, including Bridge Data Centres, Digital Halo, and Aolani, due to heightened regulatory uncertainty.

item.title: Google’s patent for custom AI video feeds paints a bleak picture of entertainment’s future
item.description: Google's 'My Channel' patent details a system that utilizes user demographic, geolocation, and viewing history to generate personalized AI-driven video feeds. The technology includes concepts for creating digital avatars of users to feature them as protagonists in AI-generated narrative content.

item.title: NY Gov. Kathy Hochul signs a bill banning AI chatbot toys for five years, starting in February; California Gov. Gavin Newsom signed a four-year ban in September (NBC News)
item.description: New York Governor Kathy Hochul signed a five-year ban on the manufacturing and sale of toys powered by generative AI chatbots, effective this coming February. This move follows California, further expanding state-level regulatory restrictions on AI-integrated consumer products for children.

item.title: Nvidia Agrees to Pay $290M to Settle Investor Lawsuit Over Crypto Mining Sales
item.description: Nvidia has agreed to a $290 million settlement to resolve a class-action lawsuit filed by investors, who alleged the company misled shareholders regarding the proportion of gaming GPU revenue driven by crypto mining during the 2017 boom. The case, which survived multiple legal challenges including Supreme Court dismissal of Nvidia's appeal, awaits preliminary court approval.

item.title: How the Trump administration determined Jensen Huang is not a national security threat
item.description: US Attorney General Todd Blanche concluded that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang poses no national security risk without conducting a formal investigation, relying on findings from probe into clients like Super Micro and Megaspeed. This decision facilitated Huang's reinstatement by the Trump administration, despite bipartisan Congressional pushback demanding more rigorous scrutiny ahead of his scheduled testimony.

item.title: US chip-access curbs and anti-distillation measures are reportedly already slowing Chinese AI labs
item.description: Restrictions on remote access to advanced chips and anti-distillation defenses from US-based model providers are widening the development gap between Chinese AI labs and US incumbents. Estimates from DeepSeek indicate a potential nine-month lag without distillation, forcing firms like Moonshot AI and Alibaba to pivot toward domestic silicon and intensified internal RL research.

item.title: WhatsApp now lets you schedule messages in group and individual chats
item.description: Meta's WhatsApp has launched a global message scheduling feature, allowing users to schedule texts, images, and videos between 10 minutes and 14 days in advance via a long-press on the send button. The messages will execute even while the device is offline, closing the utility gap with Telegram and Signal.

item.title: Sources: a16z is in talks to raise ~$20B across its next set of funds; its last set, announced in January at $15B+, later grew to $20B+ with three add-ons (Lucinda Shen/Axios)
item.description: Venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz is in talks to raise about $20 billion across its next set of funds, Axios Pro has learned from three sources familiar. Why it matters: Megafunds are raising at an accelerated clip as AI demands larger and faster checks.

item.description: Nvidia chip sellers are seeking new buyers for the semiconductor giant's hardware, three people told CNBC, after the Trump administration tightened rules to curb Chinese companies' remote access to the most advanced artificial-intelligence systems. Companies have put an unusually high volume of Nvidia graphics processing units, or GPUs, on the market since new measures restricting Chinese companies renting access to advanced Nvidia chips were announced on Nov. 16, the people said.
